acceptanceCriteria: A decision records whether and under which durability and rebinding rules a writer may skip the receipt prefix.
If accepted, mutation cost at 2,000 receipts is measured before and after, with duplicate-request and fork counterexamples still refused.
body:
## Observation

Found while fixing GitHub 446. After CAL-V0-059..061 reads resume from a checkpoint, but every mutation still walks the whole receipt chain: `store.Mutate` runs a request-index lookup audit and then `reader.Audit`, and lease writes run `AuditForWrite`. At 1,829 receipts one complete audit is about 1.1 s on this host, so each write costs 1-2 s and grows with history. A read that meets a pending receipt also falls back to the complete audit.

## Request

Decide whether writers may resume from a durable, verified checkpoint (the read checkpoint is deliberately best-effort and not write authority), what must be rebound for request-id replay detection (the read checkpoint omits `requests/`), and how often the complete audit must still run. Merge the two audits in `store.Mutate` where the protocol allows.

## GitHub 494 follow-up (2026-10-03)

Source: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/494 (created 2026-10-03T22:45:27Z). Reporter observed claim/heartbeat/release elapsed times of 10-41 seconds with about ten workers and 5,750 receipts on main-32aa5a3; idle read calls took 0.31-0.61 seconds. Twelve of 23 worker sessions in the 22:00 hour reportedly timed out; memory pressure (about 7 GB compressor, substantial swap) is a confounder. The report does not identify the exact executed Tasks binary. Local inspection uses official Tasks build 202 and immutable source dd8cc0ca918a80faaa041c98a783de11550b2bcc; this is not proof of reporter-runtime parity.

Deduplication: this ticket owns the existing history-scaling/performance decision. V1-0626 concerns retry visibility, not proof of a no-attempt charge. Do not call the issue's EXPIRED/no-start report a confirmed accounting defect without matching request, receipt, attempt and generation evidence. Distinguish a claim committed before caller timeout from a claim that never committed.

Current source evidence: internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go:69 invokes AuditForWrite on a cache miss, before lock acquisition; internal/tasks/journal/audit.go:109 still performs a complete audit. Its cache is in-process, so one-shot CLI calls do not share successful audits. internal/tasks/store/mutate.go performs request lookup and a second complete audit while holding the writer lock. These source facts support investigation, not latency attribution under the reported workload.

Next proof: a disposable representative 5k-receipt/10-worker reproduction, phase timing for preflight/audit/lock/write, exact binary and host conditions, same-request replay and cancellation at pre/post-commit boundaries, and an honest documented latency envelope. Do not bypass full writer verification or promote the best-effort read checkpoint to write authority. Preserve the original acceptance criteria and qualify any changed durability/rebinding contract independently. No load test was run against the canonical live queue.

Additional bounded source observation: `leaseWrite` at immutable dd8cc0c internal/tasks/store/lease_write.go:224 allows up to 16 prepare/commit rounds; `SNAPSHOT_MOVED` invalidates the whole preparation and triggers another full audit. Concurrent independent writers can therefore amplify preparation cost even though lease audits are outside the lock. Measure restart count as well as lock wait; a global-lock-only diagnosis is unproven.

## Bounded local measurements 2026-10-04

Generation 245 used disposable immutable-dd8cc0c source fixtures, not the canonical queue. After preserving an initial harness compilation failure and repairing only a fixture Repository field, in-process store.Lease with 2,000 audited receipts and one worker measured claim 1444.453 ms (lock hold 124.591 ms), renew 1414.065 ms (97.627 ms), release 1413.923 ms (113.755 ms); one lock acquisition each, final journal audit PASS. This is one sample per verb, not a percentile or 10-worker reproduction.

Accounting controls: pre-entry cancellation and same-request replay did not change accounting. An admitted external-agent claim whose caller launched no process expired; the next distinct claim changed retryCount from 0 to 1. This is the existing external-lease admission behavior, not proof of a phantom supervised attempt. OS crash/restart and supervised-start controls remain NOT_RUN.

Host load/swap, exact audit/restart phase timing, 5k/10-worker, installed CLI parity and causal attribution remain unqualified. No production optimization or changed durability contract. Next bounded diagnostic must measure scaling/concurrency and preparation retries while preserving all writer verification; this ticket remains OPEN.

## Controlled 5k/ten-worker attribution 2026-10-04

Generation246 ran exactly two disposable instrumented cells against immutable DD8: 5,000 receipts with one worker, then ten concurrent workers (one wave, in-process store.Lease, GOMAXPROCS=2). Single worker PASS, three operations around3.1-3.2seconds each, zero restarts. Ten workers FAILED_WORKLOAD_DEADLINE: 180second workload deadline,195.05second test including final audit;8 completed of30 planned operations,9deadline errors,13unreached. Raw logs independently confirm86preparation rounds,76full audits,10cache hits and69commit SNAPSHOT_MOVED restarts.

Concurrent request-time sums (not elapsed wall time): inventory1184.236seconds, fullaudit434.819seconds, inclusivepreparation1826.333seconds, lockwait9.404seconds, inclusivecommit19.053seconds. Restarted rounds accounted for1515.979seconds of inclusivepreparation. Inventory was more expensive than fullaudit; an audit-only or lock-wait-only explanation is insufficient. This confirms repeated costly preparation under controlled contention, not exact parity with the reporter's unknown binary or separate CLI processes.

Final journal audit returned without failure after workers joined; workload still failed its deadlines. Boundary host samples:12logicalCPU,load4.79to5.40,swap3848.06MB unchanged, systemwide swapins/out deltas0. Sampling is not continuous host-health proof. Synchronous logging adds overhead; inclusive phases overlap and cannot be summed together. wire.CodeOf(context-error) emits MALFORMED for phase logging but actual errors are context deadline exceeded, not a malformed journal.

Issue 545 numbers 2026-10-04 (PR 546, merged 20:11:16Z as 0a2807b7; GitHub issue 545): on a disposable store with 7,140 receipts each mutation costs about 2.9 s; 10 concurrent fresh-process writers sit at the 30 s preparation-admission budget; a 14-writer wave completed 55 of 70 operations with 3 LOCK_TIMEOUT.
